title: Mitochondrial oxidative DNA damage and exposure to particulate air pollution in mother-newborn pairs.
ehr_evidence: We investigated maternal (n = 224) and cord blood (n = 293) from mother-newborn pairs that were enrolled in the ENVIRONAGE birth cohort; exposure to PM2.5 and PM10 was estimated by spatial temporal interpolation (Kriging) using official fixed site monitoring and CORINE land cover data combined with a dispersion model.
summary: A prospective birth cohort study of 293 mother-newborn pairs in Genk, Belgium, examining the association between prenatal exposure to particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5) and mitochondrial 8-OHdG oxidative DNA damage biomarkers in maternal and umbilical cord blood.
key_findings: For an IQR increment in PM10 exposure during the entire pregnancy, maternal mitochondrial 8-OHdG increased by 18.3% (95% CI: 5.6 to 32.4%, p = 0.004).
PM10 exposure during the third trimester was associated with a 28.1% increase in maternal 8-OHdG (95% CI: 8.6 to 51.2%, p = 0.004).

PM2.5 exposure was associated with a 13.9% increase in maternal 8-OHdG during entire pregnancy (95% CI: 0.4 to 29.4%, p = 0.04) and a 28.1% increase in the third trimester (95% CI: 3.6 to 58.4%, p = 0.02).

In umbilical cord blood, PM10 exposure during the first and second trimester was significantly associated with 8-OHdG increases of 23.0% (95% CI: 5.9 to 42.8%, p = 0.007) and 16.6% (95% CI: 1.8 to 33.5%, p = 0.03).
No significant association was observed between cord blood 8-OHdG and PM exposure during the entire pregnancy (p > 0.11).
High maternal 8-OHdG was positively correlated with mtDNA content (r = 0.44, p < 0.0001) and cord blood 8-OHdG with mtDNA content (r = 0.58, p < 0.0001).
Neither PM exposure nor 8-OHdG levels were associated with birth weight or small for gestational age.
captured_features: mtDNA content (ratio of mitochondrial to nuclear gene copies)
PM10 exposure over entire pregnancy and per trimester
PM2.5 exposure over entire pregnancy and per trimester
Maternal age, gestational age, smoking status, maternal education, alcohol consumption, season at conception
Newborn gender, date of delivery, birth weight, gestational age
pathologies_diseases: Small for gestational age (no association found)
population: 293 singleton mother-newborn pairs recruited at East-Limburg Hospital in Genk, Belgium; maternal age range 17-44 years (mean 29), recruited during pregnancy with blood samples collected after delivery.
exposure_domain: air pollution (particulate matter PM10 and PM2.5)
limitations: Mitochondrial 8-OHdG was measured only at the end of pregnancy, impairing the ability to investigate changes during the entire pregnancy.
Residual confounding by unknown factors associated with both 8-OHdG levels and ambient air pollution cannot be excluded.
